positions.text: Code Is Law but Is Code a Contract? concludes that the Indian Contract Act requirements of offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity, free consent, and legality can each be satisfied in a smart-contract interaction when interpreted in light of blockchain architecture. This directly qualifies Kaal's disruption claim. The abstract does not establish equivalent treatment elsewhere or resolve flexibility and judicial-oversight concerns.
